prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The monocular depth map depicts an outdoor residential street corridor where the camera wearer moves rapidly forward from left to right across the 5 frames, passing a white SUV parked on the right (closing from roughly 15 m in frame 1 to 3–4 m and partially cropped at the right edge in frame 2), a palm tree, utility pole, and parked white sedan on the left (closing from roughly 25–30 m in frame 1 to 3–5 m in frame 3), a roadside signboard on the far left in frame 4 (at roughly 2 m), and low-hanging tree canopy above and to the right in frames 4–5 (reaching within 2–3 m overhead). Ahead in the centre of the roadway, two pedestrians walk side-by-side about 0.5–1 m apart (one in white on the left, one in a yellow shirt on the right), facing away from and not looking toward the camera wearer as the distance to them shrinks from over 30 m in frames 1–2 to roughly 15–20 m in frame 3, 8–10 m in frame 4, and 3–4 m in frame 5, where their lower legs are partly cropped at the bottom edge. Nothing is within arm's reach (under 1 m) of the camera wearer in any frame, though the two pedestrians remain within arm's reach of each other and their arms hang near their own sides. Compared to the RGB strip, the depth map much more clearly separates foreground vertical structures—such as the utility poles, palm trunk, signboard, and overhanging branches—from the dark background foliage and buildings, and provides a continuous ground-plane distance gradient across the wet road. However, the map is unreliable on distant sky and background structures (which saturate to uniform black), loses the two pedestrians entirely in frame 1, merges the legs of the pedestrians with the ground plane in frames 3–5, and flattens thin overhead wires and porous tree leaves into solid depth blobs.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map isolates discrete vehicles and pedestrians along the street while leaving the road, buildings, poles, and trees unlabelled as black background. Across frames 1 to 3, it tracks the parked white SUV on the right (closing from ~15 m to ~4 m before exiting view in frame 3) and the parked white sedan on the left (closing from ~25–30 m in frame 1 to ~12 m in frame 2 and ~4 m in frame 3), along with smaller distant cars parked further ahead on the left and right (~25–40 m away). The two pedestrians walking side-by-side (~0.5–1 m apart, facing away from the camera wearer) are missed in frames 1–2, partially detected in frame 3 (~15–20 m ahead, where only the left person is segmented), and both segmented in frames 4 (~8–10 m ahead) and 5 (~3–4 m ahead, partly cropped at the bottom), with nothing within arm's reach of the camera wearer. This map makes it easier than the RGB alone to spot small, distant parked cars (~25–40 m ahead near the trees and roadside) and to distinguish the boundary between the two adjacent pedestrians in frames 4–5. However, it is unreliable where it splits the single white SUV in frame 2 into two overlapping 'car' masks, completely misses both pedestrians in frames 1–2 and the right-hand pedestrian in frame 3, and places tiny spurious 'car' fragments directly on top of the pedestrians' heads and shoulders in frames 3–5 due to occlusion against distant background vehicles.
descriptions.pose: The body and hand skeleton map is completely blank (uniformly black) across all 5 frames, failing to render any yellow body keypoints or magenta hand skeletons anywhere in the scene. From the RGB context, two pedestrians are present ahead on the street, walking side-by-side roughly 0.5–1 m apart with their backs turned away from the camera wearer (not looking toward the camera), as the camera wearer approaches them from roughly 30+ m away in frame 1 to 3–4 m away in frame 5. Neither pedestrian is within arm's reach of the camera wearer, though they walk within arm's reach of one another with their arms hanging down near their own hips and thighs, and their feet and lower shins are cropped out of the bottom of frame 5. Because the pose detector outputs no skeletons at all, this map contributes no spatial information beyond the RGB image and fails to capture the walkers' dorsal orientation, upright posture, or hand positions. The map is completely unreliable here, likely due to the small pixel scale of the pedestrians in frames 1–4 and the rear-facing angle and dim lighting under the tree canopy in frame 5.
